- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent mean, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast by 10–15% for the next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction for next horizon.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.7) and forecast is erratic, smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 2+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast upward by 5–8% to reflect momentum.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
